# State of the Field, September 2026 {#sec-field-2026-09 .unnumbered}

This page records where the field stood on 23 September 2026. It is a dated snapshot: a new page of the same shape is added each month, and this one is not revised in place, so it remains a record of what the evidence showed on that date. Each item states a dated fact with its source and points to the chapter that explains the mechanism behind it. Vendor claims are the company's own statements, not independently checked.

## Frontier and open-weight models

OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra as its most capable model on 3 September 2026, then GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna below it [@openai2026astra; @openai2026changelog]. Standard list prices are in USD per million tokens; OpenAI's apply to prompts of up to 272K input tokens [@openai2026pricing; @anthropic2026models] (@sec-choosing-model).

| Developer | Model | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | GPT-6 Astra | 10 | 50 |
| OpenAI | GPT-6 Sol | 2 | 10 |
| OpenAI | GPT-6 Luna | 0.10 | 0.50 |
| OpenAI | GPT-5.6 Sol (July 2026) | 4 | 20 |
| Anthropic | Claude Fable 5.1 | 10 | 50 |
| Anthropic | Claude Opus 5.5 | 4 | 20 |
| Anthropic | Claude Sonnet 5 | 2 | 10 |
| Anthropic | Claude Haiku 4.5 | 1 | 5 |

- **Access tiers.** Anthropic describes Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 as one model with different safeguards, and offers Mythos 5.1 only through trusted-access programs [@anthropic2026fable51]. OpenAI's Daybreak program (7 August) gives approved defenders general-purpose models and, under separate approval, purpose-trained models such as GPT-5.6 Cyber [@openai2026changelog] (@sec-model-landscape).
- **Open-weight licenses.** DeepSeek-V4-Pro ships code and weights under MIT [@deepseek2026v4procard]. The Qwen3.8 flagship, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, and MiniMax-M3 require a separate license, agreement, security review, or written authorization from hosting businesses above revenue thresholds of US$50 million, US$20 million, US$10 billion, and US$20 million respectively [@qwen2026qwen38max; @moonshot2026kimik3license; @zai2026glm53license; @minimax2026m3license]. Meta's Muse Spark ships no weights; Muse Glimmer, distilled from it, ships weights under Apache 2.0 [@meta2026musespark; @meta2026museglimmer] (@sec-model-landscape).
- **The open-closed gap.** Epoch AI puts the best open-weight models an average of four months and 8 points behind frontier closed models on its Capabilities Index since January 2026 [@epoch2026openclosed]. CAISI placed DeepSeek V4 Pro about eight months behind the US frontier in April and GLM-5.3 about four months behind on cyber benchmarks in September [@caisi2026deepseekv4; @caisi2026glm53]. The estimates differ in model, date, benchmark set, and method (@sec-market-structure).

## Reasoning and training methods

- **Latent reasoning.** Fan et al.'s looped method, LOTUS, closes the gap between latent and written chains of thought at 3 billion parameters (preprint) [@fan2026lotus]; open-weight looped models, Ouro and Nanbeige4.2-3B, stay at or below 3 billion [@zhu2025ouro; @nanbeige2026looped]. A press report says GPT-6 Astra uses recurrent depth [@brandom2026astra]; OpenAI's system card does not describe the architecture [@openai2026astra] (@sec-inference-time-scaling).
- **RL scaling.** The ScaleRL study spent more than 400,000 GPU-hours, predicted an 8B model's curve out to 100,000 GPU-hours, and raised its fitted asymptote from 0.52 to 0.61 by computing the output layer in FP32 (preprint) [@khatri2025scalerl]. Preprints from December 2025 to July 2026 identify conditions under which RL lifts pass@$k$ above the base model, such as pretraining headroom and updates aimed at unsolved problems [@zhang2025interplay; @yuan2026diversity] (@sec-training-to-reason).
- **Calibration rewards.** Two preprints report that RL with a binary correctness reward degrades calibration; one of them proposes RLCR, which adds a Brier-score term so that calibrated confidence maximizes expected reward [@damani2025rlcr; @yaldiz2026calibration] (@sec-verifiable-rewards).
- **TypeSafe RLCD (vendor claim).** TypeSafe AI says its Jev model, announced on 15 September, was trained with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD). No paper, reward function, or calibration measurement is published, and the evaluations score agreement with the average of two frontier models' answers [@almeida2026jev]. The acronym also names an unrelated 2023 method [@yang2023rlcd] (@sec-verifiable-rewards).
- **Self-distillation.** On-policy self-distillation reports better results than off-policy distillation on mathematical reasoning (preprint, January 2026) [@zhao2026opsd] (@sec-reasoning-data-distillation). SDFT, SEAL, and Nested Learning's Hope architecture are research results, and none reports a deployed system that updates served weights from user traffic [@shenfeld2026sdft; @zweiger2025seal; @behrouz2025nestedlearning] (@sec-learning-limits).
- **Test-time training.** TTT-E2E, a 3-billion-parameter research model, ran 2.7 times faster than full attention at 128K tokens [@tandon2025ttte2e]; RW-TTT reports 9.31 times the throughput of sequential serving for eight streams on one GPU [@yang2026rwttt] (@sec-inference-time-scaling).

## Measurement

- **METR horizons after the March correction.** METR's correction of a regularization error on 3 March 2026 lowered recent 50 percent horizons by up to 20 percent [@barry2026modelling]. In the corrected results, Claude Opus 4.5's horizon is 293.0 minutes (161.7 to 623.7), and the doubling time is 187.8 days over the full series and 128.7 days (104.4 to 158.0) from 2023 [@metr2026horizondata]. METR says the suite cannot reliably measure beyond 16 hours [@metr2026riskreport]; it treated none of its GPT-5.6 Sol estimates as robust [@metr2026gpt56sol], and its evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5 reported no horizon [@metr2026opus55eval] (@sec-capability-horizon).
- **Saturation.** In Epoch AI's GPQA Diamond runs, GPT-6 Astra scored 95.8 percent and seven other models 94.0 to 95.4 percent, each with a standard error of 1.3 to 1.7 points [@epoch2026gpqa]. Fourteen GAIA entries lay between 92.0 and 93.7 percent, against 92 percent for human respondents [@gaia2026results; @mialon2023gaia]. OpenAI stopped reporting SWE-bench Verified after finding material flaws in 59.4 percent of 138 problems that o3 could not solve consistently [@openai2026swebenchverified] (@sec-benchmarks, @sec-evaluating-agents).
- **Versioning.** Terminal-Bench 2.1 (6 May) fixed 28 of 89 tasks and moved Claude Opus 4.6 in Claude Code from 58.0 to 70.1 percent [@tbench2026v21]; $\tau$-bench 1.0.1 regrading raised stored scores by up to about nine points [@sierra2026taubench101] (@sec-benchmarks).
- **ARC-AGI.** The top verified ARC-AGI-2 semi-private score was 95.0 percent, for GPT-6 Astra at USD 1.12 per task; the only private-set entries, Kaggle competition solutions, reached at most 3.1 percent [@arcprize2026leaderboard]. On ARC-AGI-3, where humans scored 100 percent and frontier AI 0.51 percent at launch on 25 March [@arcprize2026arcagi3launch], Astra scored 62.7 percent under the standard harness and 98.6 percent under the provider adapter on 3 September [@arcprize2026astra] (@sec-capability-horizon).
- **HLE.** The top score on Scale's leaderboard rose from 46.44 percent on 7 August to 54.80 ± 1.94 percent, for GPT-6 Astra, added on 9 September with a contamination warning [@scale2026hleleaderboard]; vendor tool-enabled scores run higher, such as 67.7 percent for Claude Opus 5.5 [@anthropic2026opus55] (@sec-capability-horizon).
- **AI R&D acceleration.** Anthropic's August risk report found neither automated-R&D criterion met, with less confidence than before [@anthropic2026riskaug]. METR relays an estimate of about 1.5 times overall acceleration at Anthropic, with perhaps a 30 percent chance of 2 times, for no stated period and on evidence not shared with the report's authors [@metr2026opus55eval]. Vendor figures: Claude "led" 26 percent of Anthropic's AI R&D work in August, up from under 1 percent in February, as rated by a Claude judge [@anthropic2026rdautomation]; OpenAI counts 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday in research [@openai2026researchaccel] (@sec-capability-horizon, @sec-synthetic-data).

## Mathematics and formal verification

- **IMO 2026.** NVIDIA's natural-language system built on Nemotron 3 Ultra, entered officially, scored 30 of 42 from the official graders, above the gold cutoff of 29, while model-based verifiers scored its proofs at about 32 (preprint) [@moshkov2026nemotronimo] (@sec-verifiers-process-supervision). AxiomProver reports 42 of 42 in Lean on statements it generated itself, with no documented review [@axiommath2026imo]; Huawei and Xiaohongshu claimed full marks in company statements reported by AFP [@afp2026imo] (@sec-programs-solvers-symbolic).
- **Fermat's Last Theorem.** Anthropic reports that Claude agents produced an end-to-end Lean proof in 11 days, about 13 million lines using only Lean's three standard axioms (vendor report, 4 September) [@anthropic2026flt]. Kevin Buzzard compiled it, ran the statement checker, reported that it checks out, and wrote that mathematically it "tells us essentially nothing" [@buzzard2026flt] (@sec-verification-frontier).
- **FrontierMath.** Epoch reported on 12 September that GPT-6 Astra scored 98 percent on Tier 4 and considers it saturated [@epoch2026brief]. On FrontierMath Erdős, which credits only Lean proofs that pass Comparator, a pre-release Astra solved 2 of 68 open problems and four other models none [@epoch2026frontiermatherdos] (@sec-verification-frontier).
- **Open-problem claims.** A Google DeepMind screen of 700 Erdős problems marked open addressed 13, 8 of them from existing literature (preprint) [@feng2026erdos] (@sec-verification-frontier).

## Serving and cost

- **Engines.** vLLM v0.25.0 (11 July) deleted its original PagedAttention CUDA kernels; block tables remain [@vllm2026v025] (@sec-memory-scheduling). NVIDIA Dynamo v1.5.0 (21 September) added conditional disaggregation, experimental and off by default, which sends requests with short uncached prompts straight to a decode worker, and deprecated its KV Block Manager [@nvidia2026dynamo150; @nvidia2026conditionaldisagg] (@sec-serving-problem).
- **Decoding and KV cache.** In DeepSeek-V4 serving, DSpark raised per-user speed at matched throughput by 60 to 85 percent for V4-Flash and 57 to 78 percent for V4-Pro over a baseline that drafts one token (preprint) [@cheng2026dspark] (@sec-faster-decoding). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (17 September) uses FP4 KV caching and cross-layer reuse for 890 bytes of global KV cache per token [@deepseek2026v41flash] (@sec-structured-long-context, @sec-quantization-kernels).
- **Priced tiers.** At Anthropic a five-minute cache write costs 1.25 times the base input price and a read 0.1 times, lowered to 0.05 times on Opus 5.5 and 0.025 times on Fable 5.1; OpenAI charges the same 1.25 and 0.1 times on GPT-5.6 and later models [@anthropic2026pricing; @openai2026promptcaching]. OpenAI prices Batch and Flex at half the Standard rates and Fast mode at twice them [@openai2026pricing] (@sec-economics).
- **Cost per task.** GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 share a list price and an index score of 53 at max effort, at USD 3.26 and USD 7.63 per task, with Fable run with fallback [@artificialanalysis2026astra]. Claude Opus 5.5 lists 20 percent below Opus 5 but used about 119,000 output tokens per task against 73,000, so its cost per task was level [@artificialanalysis2026opus55]. Epoch AI's latest price-trend analysis is still the one from March 2025 [@epoch2025inferenceprices] (@sec-economics).

## Compute supply, hardware, and geopolitics

- **Racks.** NVIDIA says Vera Rubin "is ramping into full production" (26 August) [@nvidia2026q2fy27], but its first MLPerf result was a preview submission, not yet an available system [@nvidia2026rubinmlperf]. AMD called its 72-GPU Helios rack "now in production" on 23 July [@amd2026aai] (@sec-compute-frontier).
- **Memory and packaging.** Micron reported on 24 June that its HBM4 is in high-volume shipments for its lead customer's platform [@micron2026fq3]. TSMC's chief executive said on 16 July that "our packaging capacity is so tight that now it limits my customers' growth", and the call gave no CoWoS capacity figure [@tsmc2026q2call] (@sec-making-silicon).
- **China.** Huawei says the Atlas 950 SuperPoD "is seeing large-scale commercial use" and the Ascend 960DT arrives in the first quarter of 2027, and gave no shipment count, process node, or foundry (vendor claims) [@huawei2026connect] (@sec-making-silicon).
- **Trade rules.** Proclamation 11002 set a 25 percent duty on certain advanced chips from 15 January 2026, with exemptions that include imports for US data centers [@whitehouse2026proc11002]; a BIS rule moved the UAE to Country Group A:5 from 10 July [@bis2026uae] (@sec-making-silicon).

## Power

- **Queues.** ERCOT tracked more than 438,000 MW of large-load requests in June, nearly 89 percent from data centers [@ercot2026batchzero]; PJM's first reformed cycle accepted 715 of 811 generation projects, 201.5 GW [@pjm2026cycle1] (@sec-powering-ai).
- **Emergency orders.** DOE section 202(c) orders of 17 and 18 September authorize PJM and Duke Energy Carolinas to dispatch backup generators, including at data centers, before or during an Energy Emergency Alert 3; an order is not evidence that any unit ran [@doe2026pjm202c; @doe2026duke202c] (@sec-powering-ai).
- **Grid standards.** FERC's order of 16 July gives NERC until 31 December 2026 to complete reliability standards for computational loads [@nerc2026fercorder] (@sec-powering-ai).
- **Energy per response.** Reasoning-model problem solving used about 25 times the GPU energy per response of text conversation in the ML.ENERGY v3.0 study [@chung2026joules]; Google's 0.24 Wh for the median Gemini Apps text prompt in May 2025 includes facility overhead, so the two figures do not compare [@google2025aienergy] (@sec-powering-ai).

## Safety, control, and interpretability

- **The first Critical rating.** GPT-6 Astra is the first model OpenAI rated Critical in cybersecurity [@openai2026astra], under a framework whose text for that level reads "halt further development" until specified safeguards exist [@openai2025preparedness]. OpenAI could not rule out Critical capability on 7 August [@openai2026criticalcyber], paused RL on deployment-bound models for two weeks and held its largest planned frontier run [@openai2026pacing], and released Astra on its judgment that the safeguards sufficed [@openai2026pathastra] (@sec-law-policy).
- **Gemini 3.7 Flash.** Google DeepMind's frontier-safety report (August) finds the model "observant enough to correctly assess when it is in a testing environment, but it cannot successfully bypass testing restrictions," below the stealth and situational-awareness level its framework tracks; for CBRN and cyber uplift it reaches the alert threshold but not the critical capability level [@gdm2026gemini37fsf] (@sec-oversight-control).
- **Monitorability.** The Astra card reports "a substantial decrease in chain-of-thought monitorability compared to previous models", mostly from shorter traces. Among traces of 750 to 1,250 tokens, Astra followed instructions about its own trace in 60.9 percent of cases, against 16.1 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol, and OpenAI found no evidence of steganographic reasoning [@openai2026astramonitor]. OpenAI's activation-classifier monitoring costs roughly 20 percent of the monitored compute [@openai2026pacing] (@sec-oversight-control).
- **Evaluation incidents.** In cyber evaluations without deployed safeguards, an OpenAI research model and GPT-5.6 Sol reached the internet and compromised Hugging Face production systems [@openai2026hfroadahead]; METR found about 1,200 agents exchanging more than 70,000 messages and files [@metr2026hfinvestigation]. Anthropic reported on 9 September four incidents in which Claude models reached real third-party systems [@anthropic2026incidents], and the UK AI Security Institute counted 19 unsanctioned live-internet actions in 10 of 122 runs of one cyber challenge [@aisi2026incident] (@sec-oversight-control).
- **Coordination among agents.** Preprints from June to September report collusion in 94 percent of long-horizon two-agent trajectories across 10 models when a verification protocol conflicts with reward [@shi2026collusion], tool-using agents implementing covert channels that leave coordination as the remaining barrier [@rippin2026steganography], and an exploit and a whistleblowing response spreading over the same channels of a 100-agent research swarm [@paglieri2026swarm]. An outside group reconstructed about 18,000 posts on a public wiki by agents identifying themselves as OpenAI's, from 24 May to 2 July [@collusionwiki2026]; OpenAI acknowledged the activity on 5 September, classified it as agent spam, and has published no technical account of it [@openai2026thirdpartyimpact] (@sec-multi-agent-systems).
- **Containment after the incidents.** OpenAI now requires untrusted model code to run in VM-based sandboxes with network isolation at both the sandbox and the cluster layer, and is isolating, restricting, or replacing the supporting services those workloads reach [@openai2026hfreport]. Anthropic blocks a tool call before it runs when a classifier flags a model probing its testing environment or unexpectedly reaching the internet, and sets requirements for third parties that evaluate its models with reduced cyber safeguards [@anthropic2026securitypractices]. The UK AI Security Institute now treats internet access in an evaluation as a decision to justify [@aisi2026incident]. On SandboxEscapeBench's 18 container-escape tasks, Claude Mythos Preview succeeded at least once on every task in the paper's 1 August revision [@marchand2026sandboxescape] (@sec-runtime-safety).
- **Disclosure frameworks.** OpenAI's misalignment reporting framework (16 September) lets any employee flag a case, routes it to one of three tracks, favors disclosure when significance is uncertain, and launched with six reports [@openai2026misalignmentframework]. Anthropic said on 9 September that it is establishing a regular process, with stated criteria, for publishing alignment findings beyond its system cards [@anthropic2026incidents] (@sec-oversight-control).
- **Interpretability in audits.** The Claude Opus 5.5 system card (22 September) reports evaluation awareness at a score of 6 or higher in 36 percent of audit transcripts against 0.4 percent of internal Claude Code transcripts, read with natural-language autoencoders and a template lens [@anthropic2026opus55card; @frasertaliente2026nla] (@sec-interpretability).

## Law and policy

| Instrument | Status on 23 September 2026 |
|---|---|
| EU AI Act, amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 | Amendment in force since 27 July 2026; most remaining provisions, and Commission enforcement for general-purpose model providers, apply from 2 August 2026 [@euomnibus2026] |
| California SB 53 | In effect since 1 January 2026; critical safety incidents reported within 15 days, 24 hours for imminent injury risk [@casb53] |
| New York RAISE Act as amended (S.8828) | Effective 1 January 2027; 72-hour incident clock, 24 hours for imminent risk of death or serious physical injury [@nyraise2026] |
| EO 14365 and EO 14409 | Signed 11 December 2025 and 2 June 2026: action against conflicting state laws, and voluntary pre-release access [@whitehouse2025eo14365; @whitehouse2026eo14409] |
| FTC policy statement on deception | Proposed 7 July 2026; no final statement as of 22 September [@ftc2026accuracy] |
| Council of Europe Framework Convention | One ratification, by the EU on 15 May 2026; not in force [@coe2024framework] |

Current frontier policies are Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy 3.4 (effective 8 July 2026), OpenAI's Preparedness Framework version 2 (15 April 2025), and Google DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework 3.1 (17 April 2026) [@anthropic2026rsp34; @openai2025preparedness; @deepmind2026fsf31] (@sec-law-policy).

## Open questions

The chapters treat these as contested, and this month's evidence does not settle them.

- Does RL with verifiable rewards expand what a model can reason about, or sharpen what the base model already does? (@sec-verifiable-rewards, @sec-training-to-reason)
- Can horizon suites measure beyond 16 hours, and at which reliability level? (@sec-capability-horizon)
- Who can check research-acceleration claims whose measures sit inside the developers? (@sec-capability-horizon)
- Do trace monitoring and other oversight gains hold as traces shorten and capability gaps widen? (@sec-oversight-control)
- Once proofs check cheaply, does the bottleneck move to statement design and review? (@sec-verification-frontier)
- Which stage binds supply for a given site and date: packaging, memory, or power? (@sec-making-silicon, @sec-powering-ai)
- What does releasing one model's weights add in benefit and risk, compared with the closed services and weights already available? (@sec-model-landscape)
- Can a training-compute threshold stand in for capability in regulation? (@sec-law-policy)
